extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, agency rulewriters, lawyers, NGOs, and public commenters on federal immigration rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to a Departments' rulemaking delaying parts of and withdrawing amendatory instructions from the Security Bars Final Rule; explains legal and practical reasons for withdrawing specific regulatory amendments, responds to public comments, and assesses APA compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw amendatory instructions that conflict with intervening rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendatory instructions that would overwrite or reinstate provisions removed or amended by subsequent rules should be withdrawn to avoid creating conflicting text, inconsistent and confusing terminology, and unjustified reversion without observing APA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments concluded that several amendatory instructions to the Security Bars Final Rule (e.g., instructions 4, 6, 8, 12, 14, and related authority citations 5, 7, 13) must be withdrawn because intervening rules amended or rescinded the very provisions those instructions would alter; allowing those instructions to take effect would produce inconsistencies in the CFR, editorial notes from OFR, and potential interference with implementation (see Sections II.E and III.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid codifying obsolete regulatory language (do not reintroduce rescinded provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add back regulatory provisions that were removed by later rules (for example, provisions implementing the TCT bar) because that would codify obsolete language and establish procedures for bars that no longer exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the Lawful Pathways Final Rule rescinded provisions such as 8 CFR 208.30(e)(5)(iii) and 1208.30(g)(1); if amendatory instructions 4 and 12 were not withdrawn, the Security Bars Final Rule would reinsert those provisions and create procedures for a TCT bar that the Departments rescinded (see 88 FR 31314 and discussion in II.E.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency between discretionary and mandatory screening provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid having coexisting CFR provisions where some make consideration of statutory bars during credible fear screenings discretionary and others make it mandatory, because that would create irreconcilable procedural standards and screening outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, current paragraph (ii) of 8 CFR 208.30(e)(5) allows an AO to 'may consider' mandatory bars, while the Security Bars Final Rule's amendatory instruction would add a paragraph requiring application of mandatory bars (paragraph (iv)), leading to different screening standards (e.g., 'significant possibility' v. 'more likely than not' for torture) and conflicting placement of positive determinations (AWO proceedings v. section 240 removal or USCIS jurisdiction). Such irreconcilable provisions justify withdrawing the conflicting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not instruct OFR to 'revise' CFR paragraphs that no longer exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must avoid amendatory instructions that direct the Office of the Federal Register to 'revise' specific CFR paragraphs where those paragraphs were removed by intervening rules, because OFR cannot revise non-existent paragraphs and would likely add editorial notes indicating agency error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendatory instructions 4, 8, and 12 originally instructed OFR to revise five specific paragraphs (e.g., 8 CFR 208.30(e)(5)(i)(A) and (B), 1003.42(d)(1), 1208.30(g)(1)(ii)) that later rules removed; the Document Drafting Handbook explains OFR may add editorial notes of agency error in such situations, which would create confusion and questions about validity and effect of the text (see discussion and citation to DDH at 6-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ability to use expedited removal system (avoid regulatory changes that impede operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not implement changes that would jeopardize the Departments' ability to operate the expedited removal system; conflicting or confusing regulatory text can impede operational use of expedited removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments determined that allowing the Security Bars Final Rule to take effect without withdrawing conflicting instructions could put their ability to use expedited removal at risk because of confusing CFR text and editorial notes that interfere with processing and adjudication under expedited procedures (see Section II.E introduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve clear de novo Immigration Judge review of AO credible fear determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text should clearly provide that Immigration Judges review asylum officers' credible fear determinations de novo, including review of any application of bars to asylum or withholding of removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EOIR amended 8 CFR 1003.42(d) to explicitly state IJ de novo review includes review of an AO's application of any bars pursuant to 8 CFR 208.30(e)(5); because amendatory instruction 8 would have instructed OFR to revise a paragraph that no longer exists, withdrawing instruction 8 preserves clarity that IJs can review AOs' application of bars (see II.E.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit regulatory text to necessary provisions for substantive public-health-related clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdraw ancillary procedural amendments that are unnecessary to effectuate the substantive public health-related provisions the rule intends to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments concluded that amendments concerning credible fear procedures and third-country removals were unnecessary to effectuate the Security Bars Final Rule's substantive clarifications about public-health-related 'danger to the security' bars; withdrawing those instructions avoids confusion while allowing substantive clarifications to take effect (see III and B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating confusion about third-country removal legal tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory amendments must not imply that in all third-country-removal circumstances aliens are only screened for a likelihood of torture (CAT) and not for the likelihood of persecution (statutory withholding), when both tests may be relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Security Bars Final Rule's proposed revisions to 8 CFR 208.16(f) and 1208.16(f) would have required consideration of likelihood of torture in the third country but did not include the statutory withholding (persecution) test, which could mislead readers; therefore, the Departments withdrew those amendments to avoid incorrect impressions and interference with DHS's ability to effect third-country removals under INA 241(b) and existing immigration procedures (see III.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the substantive clarifications of 'danger to the security' bars to public-health criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When retained, substantive provisions should clarify that statutory 'danger to the security of the United States' bars encompass certain emergency public health concerns (e.g., exhibiting symptoms, exposure during incubation/contagion, joint designation of epidemic regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments are implementing the Security Bars Final Rule's clarifying substantive provisions at 8 CFR 208.13(c)(10), 1208.13(c)(10), 8 CFR 208.16(d)(2), and 1208.16(d)(2), which introduce criteria such as exhibiting disease symptoms or exposure during incubation/contagion and allow joint designation of regions experiencing epidemics (see III.C). These substantive clarifications remain in effect while conflicting procedural amendments are withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfy APA notice-and-comment and effective-date requirements (or explain exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking must comply with the Administrative Procedure Act's notice-and-comment requirements and the general 30-day delayed effective date unless an exception applies; agencies should document solicitation and consideration of comments and justify any delays or exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments explain that this rulemaking satisfies APA notice-and-comment because they previously sought and considered public comments in the multiple delay IFRs and that the Departments considered and explained earlier delays (e.g., two-year and one-year delays) to assess inconsistencies; the preamble cites 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A)-(B) and 553(d) and summarizes how comments were solicited and considered (see V.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate comments on delay/procedure from comments on substantive merits
rubrics_metrics.description: In responding to public comments, distinguish feedback addressing procedural matters (e.g., effective date, delay) from comments addressing the substantive merits of the underlying rule, and point to prior responses where substantive issues were already addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Departments note that many commenters addressed the merits of the Security Bars Final Rule (issues previously considered in the NPRM and final rule responses), while others specifically addressed further delay; the Departments responded by reiterating prior explanations and focusing the current rulemaking on technical/technical-non-substantive changes to avoid re-litigating the rule's merits (see IV and responses throughout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and respond to concerns about less-restrictive alternatives, discrimination, due process, and treaty obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should evaluate commenters' claims that a rule is overly broad, discriminatory, violates due process or non-refoulement obligations, or that less-restrictive public-health measures could achieve the government's aims, and respond explaining why the rule does or does not adopt alternatives or raise those legal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble summarizes numerous public comments raising these concerns (e.g., calls to use testing/isolation instead of bars, allegations of discrimination or treaty violations) and states the Departments' disagreement and reference to prior responses in the Security Bars Final Rule; where credible fear amendments implicated burdens of proof or procedural fairness, the Departments withdrew those amendatory instructions to avoid codifying disputed screening standards (see IV.B and related responses).
